To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proportion of time spent on a component of a concurrent response-independent variable-interval schedule is a function of the relative rates of the two concurrent variable-interval reinforcement schedules and of the changeover time.

the proportion of session time spent in a schedule component is a decreasing function of changeover delay and an increasing function of the difference between reinforcement rates for the two schedule components.

(a) the proportion of the session time spent in a component is a function of the relative rate of reinforcement in the component, and (b) changeover delay is a function of both the relative rates of the concurrent schedules and of the changeover delays.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of the independent variable of changeover delay in the concurrent variable-interval schedule are similar to the effects of the same independent variable on concurrent variable-interval response-dependent schedules of reinforcement.

the effects of changeover delay and relative reinforcement rate in response-independent concurrent variable-interval reinforcement schedules are similar to their effects in response-dependent concurrent variable-interval schedule of reinforcement.

the effects of relative rate and changeover rate on concurrent performance are similar regardless of whether the reinforcement is arranged by a response-dependent schedule of variable interval or a response-independent schedule of variable interval.
